recap.workouts:
CAn4, ridden exactly as revised this morning: the six Zone 4 reps in, the 30' Z2 tail out. 61:54, 34.2 km, load 50 against a planned 86, avg 158 W, avg HR 132, max 159. Paired cleanly to the planned session. The 68.5% compliance figure is scored against the original 90' version including the tail I told you to cut — it reads as a shortfall and isn't one.

Warm-up: 10:03 @ 136 W, HR 115 avg, max 129. Honest Z1.

The six reps, target band 248–283 W, every one of them 2:28–2:29 long:
rep 1 — 264 W, HR 144 avg, peak 153
rep 2 — 264 W, 146, peak 156
rep 3 — 264 W, 147, peak 157
rep 4 — 264 W, 148, peak 158
rep 5 — 264 W, 148, peak 159
rep 6 — 264 W, 149, peak 159

264 W is 112% of the new FTP — dead centre of the Z4 band. ERG-locked, so the watt-for-watt steadiness is the trainer's doing, but six full reps with no early stop and no shortened rep is entirely yours.

The HR story, and it's a good one. Peaks climbed 153 → 156 → 157 → 158 → 159 and then stopped: rep 6 matched rep 5 exactly at 159, which is your bike LTHR to the beat. A Zone 4 set that tops out AT threshold heart rate and then flattens instead of climbing through it is a set that never went into a hole. Average HR across the reps rose only five beats end to end.

The recoveries are the sharper read, because that was the gate I gave you this morning. HR bottomed at 118 · 121 · 121 · 123 · 123 between reps — roughly 30 beats shed every single time, and only five beats of upward creep across the whole set. "Stop at four only if HR stops dropping between reps." It never stopped dropping. Riding all six was the right call, made on the bike, on the evidence.

One number not to misread: the work reps show +9 to +10% decoupling. On a 2.5-minute rep your HR is still climbing when the rep ends, by construction — that figure is lag, not drift. Reps this short cannot be judged that way; the peak-HR trend across the set is the honest instrument, and it flattened.

Then 11:53 at 120 W to spin down rather than stepping straight off the bike. Zone 1, essentially free, and it does not quietly put the tail back on.

Nothing came through from the phone today — no note, no log. The ride told the story on its own.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (603 s warm-up, then 148 s / 302 s six times). The Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox this evening, so the numbers above are per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing is estimated.
recap.takeaways:
1) ADAPT: no-op — CAn4 EXECUTED to the revised prescription, and the week's arithmetic finally lands where it was supposed to. Mon–Fri ran 376, today added 50, Sunday adds nothing. Week 8 closes near 426 against week 7's 456 — roughly 6.6% lighter than the build week it was meant to deload from, and better than the 431 I projected at 06:15. This is the first deload of the block that actually deloaded. That was the boss fight, and it got won on the last day of the week.

2) Endurance verdict: clean, high confidence. Six identical reps at 264 W, peak HR flattening at LTHR rather than climbing through it, ~30 beats shed in every recovery, load 50 for 15 minutes of Zone 4. There is no fatigue flag anywhere in this trace. Consequence: proceed — nothing here needs protecting.

3) On the record, since it has been the theme of the week: you overrode me Thursday and Friday and the files came back clean both times. Today I moved toward you at 06:15 and you rode the compromise precisely as agreed — reps in, tail out. That is the version of this that works. Both tunes banked, the anchors are now measured rather than inherited, and the weekend is intact.

4) Tomorrow is the honest test of whether the deload worked. Mandate §3 red flag: deep soreness plus a subjective slog on the Sunday of a deload week means it didn't. If that is how you wake up, say so — it goes straight into Week 9's plan-gen rather than being let slide.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.

recovery.bannerTitle: FULL REST — and today that's the prescription, not the leftover (24)
recovery.bannerSub: Nothing on the plan today and nothing to argue about. Three things worth knowing before tomorrow: the week actually deloaded (~426 load vs week 7's 456, −6.6%) and Form has climbed −25.8 → −23.7 → −20.7, so the training side is moving the right way; but sleeping HR is elevated for a seventh straight morning and respiratory rate is now the strongest reading of the whole stretch, and last night stopped at 03:29 for 6.1 h asleep. A lighter week that produced a LOWER readiness number is the part that doesn't fit a training explanation.
recovery.note: Readiness 24 — the lowest of the block, off 27 twice. Here's the honest tension, and I'd rather name it than smooth it: the load side of the ledger finally did what it was supposed to. Week 8 closed ~426 against week 7's 456, ATL is falling, Form is the shallowest it has been in ten days, and yesterday's CAn4 was a clean six-rep set with HR flattening exactly at LTHR and ~30 beats shed in every recovery. None of that is a fatigued athlete. And yet the overnight signals went the wrong way across that same week: sleeping HR 58 → 61 → 63 → 64 → 64 → 63 → 65 (3-night smooth 64.0 vs a 57.5 baseline) and respiratory rate now 14.4 against 13.4, worse than yesterday and worse than Thursday. Two autonomic markers drifting up THROUGH a genuine deload is not what accumulated training load looks like — it's what an early bug, or life stress, or a hot bedroom looks like. Wrist temp ticked 35.61 → 35.90 but is still under the flag threshold, so I'm not calling it illness; I'm calling it watch-it, second week running. What I'd weight today: sleep. 6.11 h ending at 03:29 is the second truncated night in three, the 7-night average is 7.2 h against a need of 8, and both exports this morning carry the identical stage list, so 03:29 is a real wake, not a sync artefact. Rest is already the plan — the only thing you can actually get wrong today is treating a rest day as a free day and going to bed late again. Tomorrow opens the Week 9 build; the deload earned that, but the overnight numbers haven't yet agreed, and today's plan-gen should hear from you how you actually feel before it commits.

_prevNote: Revised at 06:15 after Sascha challenged the 05:52 version. Two corrections on the record. FIRST: my original argument was that yesterday's RAn4 had something at stake and today's CAn4 does not. That was rubbish — on Friday I argued the exact opposite, that RAn4 had no deliverable left, and I reversed it afterwards to make today sound different. Withdrawn. The honest difference between the two sessions is size, not stakes: RAn4 was load 37 with 10 minutes of hard time; CAn4 as written is planned load 86, with 15 minutes of Z4 plus a 30-minute Z2 tail. SECOND, his hypothesis — that training LESS this week is why sleeping HR is no longer suppressed — deserves more credit than I gave it. The timing genuinely fits: sleeping HR averaged 58.6 across week 7 when training was heaviest, and 62.2 across this week. Losing the plasma-volume expansion that training maintains is a real mechanism and it moves within days. He was also right about wrist temperature on Thursday when I was the alarmist one. What the hypothesis does NOT survive is its own premise: he has not trained less. Mon–Fri load this week was 376 against 343 for week 7's Mon–Fri, a 10% INCREASE, and ATL rose 68.4 → 74.5 across the deload. What fits his story badly is respiratory rate — detraining does not raise breathing rate. What fits mine badly is that he feels fine and executed cleanly two days running. Neither reading can be separated with the data on disk, and the HR/RR figures are window-contaminated by roughly two hours of the previous night, so both deserve less confidence than a single number implies. THE TIEBREAK is therefore the thing not in dispute: ride CAn4 as written and week 8 finishes at 462 against week 7's 456 — a deload heavier than the build week it followed, which is the week-4 failure repeating regardless of whose HR story is correct. REVISED CALL: ride the six Z4 reps, skip the 30-minute Z2 tail. That lands the week near 431, an actual 5% reduction, keeps the stimulus that is the session's entire point, and finally lets the week do its one job. Stop at four reps only if HR stops dropping in the recoveries — on the body, not on a dashboard number. Sunday stays full rest.
